steps.text: Melt butter in a medium saucepan over low heat. Add flour and whisk until smooth.
Add milk a little at a time, whisking well after each addition. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and cook, stirring, until thickened.
Stir in beef and cayenne; cook until warmed through.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast
raw_recipe.description: Chipped beef is a classic military dish made with dried beef in a thick and creamy white sauce seasoned with cayenne pepper that's served over toast.

video.description: Want a simple lunch or dinner meal that’s delicious and easy? Cream chipped beef on toast could be it! Butter, flour, milk, and beef mix together with a little cayenne pepper for some spice. Add on top of toast and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
video.name: Creamed Chipped Beef on Toast

review.reviewBody: My whole family just love it!! Instead of using jar of dried beef I just use 8oz. thin slices of beef lunchmeat "Budding" and it a lot cheaper!! Not salty at all and you don't even have to rinse!! You must try it and believe me, you won't be disappointed!!!!

My husband loved it, my 12 year old son declared it his "favorite meal", and we all wished I'd made more.
The funny thing is-after reading the reviews, I boiled the jarred dried beef a minute, then rinsed it off...then we all had to ADD salt (and pepper) to our portion...Go Figure!

I have been making SOS for years and reading the reviews here, the same thing keeps getting my attention - that it doesn’t have much flavor. In my opinion this recipe is missing a few items that , to me, are essential. I always “frizz” the beef aka fry the beef is a little butter until the ends of the pieces start to curl. I add some finely chopped onion to your individual taste. I remove the beef and onion, then make the white sauce. For a great flavor blast add some Old Bay to your taste and most importantly, add Worcestershire sauce. This recipe counteracts the bland!
I've been making this for 55 years. I gently sautee the torn beef in the butter and continue as stated. I love this for Dinner with Green Beans—it's the perfect combo!

I did not try this recipe as this is not the SOS (S**T on a Shingle) that I grew up with. My mom never used measurements in her life! She would melt butter in a skillet and cook the beef (Buddig) until it was a bit shriveled. Then added enough flour to soak up all the butter. Once that is done, she would add the milk slowly until it thickened up. Add salt & pepper. As a child and then as a mother myself, I would use a lot of the Buddig for a family of 5. Like 12 packages!!! This would take 2 sticks of butter, and about a 1/2 gallon of milk. Yes, my family loves this stuff and each of my adult children now make it for their family :)
Loved it!! I use the beef in a Jar (Armour Dried Beef) just rinse it off, and then follow the Recipe, put over Toast & when i add the milk i use my wire whip never any lumps easy, easy, easy

My dad was a pacific Marine during WWII & introduced me to SOS when I was a young kid. And believe me, “same old stuff” is NOT the Marine wordage!! Or, the Air Force, according to my husband. 😏😉 Sh$t on a Shingle fits when you’re stuck in a war zone with very little food around. That being said, the recipe is pretty decent, but is much better, in regards to origins, on very dry toast without cayenne added. And I don’t think I want to try chipped beef in a jar…Buddig Beef in a bag works for me! 😏 When it comes to traditional recipes, I am a bug for following the original recipe, & being an 11th generation Marine daughter, with a 12th generation Marine son, we make it the proper way! lol!

Good recipe, but the amount of beef is WAY off. 8 oz is far too much for the amount of sauce. I use a 2.25 oz jar of Armour beef and it's much better balanced. Also, the recipe doesn't mention soaking the beef in warm water, rinsing, and drying before chopping. Failure to do this results in VERY salty creamed chipped beef.

I've made this for more than 40 years. Family fav. Handy hint: slightly brown the butter before adding the flour, then cook the flour and butter together over med/lo heat, to brown the butter and flour some. This will take the flavor profile to a nuttier flavor, that really elevates this dish. Be sure to rinse the chipped beef before putting it into the gravy. I soak it in a bowl of cold water, after I slice the rounds into 3 sections, then squeeze dry. Taste test it, you do want some salt left in there, and if you rinse it too much, it'll be bland as heck. You may need some trial and error here. Chipped beef, marketed by Hormel and Armour, is difficult to find these days, but worth it. There are online resources.

Unlike other "reviewers," I prepared the recipe exactly as written. I used the dried beef called for, not hamburger or Walmart beef. Despite the fact that the beef label merely suggested, rather than specifying, rinsing the beef, I did not do so because the recipe never mentioned rinsing. The result was inedible because of the saltiness. If I try this again I will definitely rinse next time. Lisa, if the beef is to be rinsed, say so in the recipe. Oh, and S.O.S. definitely does not stand for "same old stuff."

I grew up eating this stuff, and I loved it. My mom made it with the stuff in the glass jar. Some years later, I got a hankering for dried beef gravy. I tried the Buddig, but it didn't seem quite the same. So, I bought some of the stuff in a jar. My gravy was so salty I didn't like it, even though it was tasty. Next time, I rinsed the beef to remove salt, but it wasn't the same. I am now watching my sodium intake and accept that I cannot eat this. I just bought some lunch meat beef to try and I will see, But I love the taste of this stuff. 3 stars for the salt.

My grandma use to make this and IF we had extra money she would put it on toasted English muffins. I however put mine on garlic bread, or just eat it out of a bowl. One of my favorite childhood dishes...

People need to read everything before starting. It clearly says to rinse the beef to remove excess salt. Only change for me is to add pepper, touch of garlic powder and serve over mashed potatoes. This is the basic recipe everyone should know for shit on a shingle
Hubby really likes this, me....not so much. Added worcestershire sauce.
We had this as children. It was an old WW2 meal. It was called sh$t on a shingle during the war. Daddy spoke of it and we ate it up. Glad to see it make a come back. Just good food.
I love a bit of heat, so I added 2 tsp Jalapeno powder to recipe. YUM This is a fond memory of the US Army cooking during the Vietnam War.

I can't believe I waited until I was so old before I made this lol I only had it once in my life, when I stayed overnight at my cousins when I was about 12yo. Loved it, but somehow forgot about it. Now its a weekly thing lol So good and so quick n easy. Thank you!!! : )
We ate this growing up because it was cheap. These days this sliced dry beef is crazy expensive! I can buy a nice rib eye steak for this price! I used to love SOS!
Everything went together easily enough and was quick to prep and prepare. My only complaint was that I didn't soak the dried beef to rid it of some of the salt. It was overwhelming.
